5
A car travels anticlockwise along a horizontal circular road of radius 12 m, as shown.
The car takes a time of 4.0 s to move from position P to position Q.
direction of
travel of car
12 m
P
road
Q
What is the magnitude of the average velocity of the car for the journey from P to Q?
A
4.2 m s–1
B
4.7 m s–1
C
6.0 m s–1
D
14 m s–1

hints: Notice positions P on the east and Q on the south with centre radii of $12 \text{ m}$ at $90^{\circ}$ - average velocity needs the straight displacement $PQ$, not the curved road.
Connect displacement to Pythagoras: $PQ$ is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with two $12 \text{ m}$ sides, so $PQ = \sqrt{12^2+12^2}$.
Divide that straight-line distance in $\text{m}$ by the given $4.0 \text{ s}$ to get magnitude in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and compare with the options - do not use $2\pi r$ arc length.
walkthrough: Identify the displacement direction: P to Q is a straight line, not the road. From the diagram the radii CP and CQ are $12 \text{ m}$ and perpendicular.
State the rule: magnitude of average velocity $= \text{displacement} / \text{time}$, where displacement $PQ$ is the hypotenuse.
Divide by time: $v_{av} = 17.0 \text{ m} / 4.0 \text{ s} \approx 4.24 \text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 4.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Note why speed differs: the three-quarter arc length $\approx 56.5 \text{ m}$ would give $\approx 14 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for average speed, which is not asked for. This is option A.

A.explanation: Displacement $PQ = \sqrt{12^2 + 12^2} \approx 17.0 \text{ m}$ divided by $4.0 \text{ s}$ gives $\approx 4.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: This is the average speed for a quarter-circle arc $\pi \times 12 / 2$ divided by $4.0 \text{ s}$, not the magnitude of displacement $PQ$ divided by time.

C.explanation: This uses $24 \text{ m}$ divided by $4.0 \text{ s}$, which treats displacement as a diameter rather than the hypotenuse $PQ$ of the $12 \text{ m}$ right triangle.

D.explanation: This is the average speed for the actual three-quarter arc $3 \times 2\pi \times 12 / 4$ divided by $4.0 \text{ s}$, not average velocity based on straight-line displacement.
